method: Fresh independent pixel review. Source inventory composed and chmod 0444 before any author report or candidate comparison. Exactly eight original-size image tool opens in one batch; no further images. Complete approved ZH/EN templates read as figure context without repeating their existing whole-text SCI/ZHEN review. Current final specs, SVG XML, frozen receipts and measured-width metadata read only. Neither code assertions nor native PASS replaced visual observation.

existingTextReview.bindingBasis: Exact retained context manifest; not reopened, repeated or newly recertified.

relationshipEvidence: each mapped ray's incident-parallel, reflection-through-model-F, contact-on-sphere, incident-connects and reflected-connects assertions
inventoryComparison.pixelJudgment: All six source incident rays remain visible, three above and three below the one solid axis. All six reach the same continuous left-facing concave mirror; their reflected paths pass through F and continue left. Six rightward incoming and six leftward outgoing arrowheads remain visible at all three widths. No focal plane or dashed optical ray has been imported. O, F and the pole are in the correct axial order; the ray crossing is in front of the mirror.
inventoryComparison.labels: O and F sit immediately above their own filled markers. P is above-right of the unique mirror/axis junction, clearly outside the backing; no other named or competing point is nearby. This remains unambiguous at 331 and 342 px.
inventoryComparison.mirrorBacking: Right-side diagonal hatches stay on the nonreflecting side and do not cross onto the illuminated left face.
inventoryComparison.modernAdditions: Straightened scan skew, regular ray spacing, regular hatches, and English paraxial/not-to-scale captions are modern aids, not numerical source facts. Tiny construction endpoints are not extra named data.
inventoryComparison.completeness: All independently inventoried points, rays, directions, line styles and relationships are accounted for.

textComparison.SCI: Actual solid reflected rays meet at the on-axis real focus in the schematic, consistent with the complete approved ZH/EN text. The broad drawn bundle is explicitly labeled Paraxial approximation and Schematic, not to scale; it is not accepted as measured exact spherical reflection or exact all-aperture focusing.
textComparison.signsUnitsAndAnswers: No numeric values, signs, units, scale ticks, or exercise-answer annotations are present. The approved lesson has zero exercises. O, F and P are point names, not asserted numeric focal distances.
textComparison.cultural: Only English explanatory captions and Latin scientific point names are visible. The old embedded figure number is omitted from the diagram; no Chinese, Cyrillic, political symbols, archival texture or invented cultural scene is copied.

widthReviews.observation: Complete nonblank frame, six paired ray paths, clear arrows and O/F/P association, no clipped line ends or captions.
Every ray and direction remains distinguishable. All three names and both English captions remain readable and inside the image.
Same complete readable structure and point association; no additional defect.

The named diagram therefore fails instructional scientific use; this is not a repeat failure of the approved lesson text.

relationshipEvidence: each mapped ray's parallel-secondary, through-D and connects assertions
inventoryComparison.pixelJudgment: Four solid incoming paths slope up-right and are parallel. Four reflected paths converge on the visible D junction and continue left; the top branch retraces the O-D-C line, the K branch is horizontal, and the remaining two extend up-left. Four incoming and four outgoing arrowheads are present. The single vertical dashed plane passes through the on-axis marked point F and the above-axis junction D. The axis is solid, unarrowed, and continuous. Mirror contacts retain the source top-to-bottom ordering and the lower contact remains without its own intended name in the spec.
inventoryComparison.mirrorBacking: Continuous left-facing concave mirror with backing hatches only to its right.
inventoryComparison.completeness: The underlying ray/point topology, directions and dash distinction match the independent source inventory. The visible labels do not provide a faithful usable association for that topology.
inventoryComparison.modernAdditions: Small-angle narrowing, regular hatches, open marker regularization, English Focal plane and Paraxial model captions are declared modern aids; no numerical source fact or exact arbitrary-angle focusing claim is added.

textComparison.geometryAndScope: The approved ZH/EN text allows approximate off-axis convergence in a small-angle narrow bundle and an approximately perpendicular focal plane. The current geometry and Paraxial model caption stay within that scope; no exact equal-distance plane or all-aperture spherical focusing is certified.
textComparison.signsUnitsAndAnswers: No numerical values, signed focal-length formula, units, ticks or answer annotations are present. Six source Latin point names are retained, with the source lower contact intentionally unnamed.
textComparison.cultural: Focal plane is translated into English. All visible text is English or Latin point names, with no copied source Chinese label, old figure number, Cyrillic, political symbol, texture or fabricated scene.

widthReviews.observation: Nonblank unclipped frame and readable glyphs do not rescue association: O is detached above-left, F is down along the dashed plane, and P sits by the lower contact rather than the pole.

The same spatial ambiguity survives normal mobile size. P visually accompanies the lower hit, F is separated far below the axial crossing, and O appears beside an upper ray. No leader ties these letters back to their markers.
Slightly larger mobile width retains exactly the detached-letter problem; this is not a sub-16px font or clipping failure.

defects.visualBasis: Independent observation of the source and all three current final previews, not acceptance of the author HOLD as truth.
defects.description: The six letters are legible, but O/F/P are not reliably associated with the scientific points. P is closer in row to the lower unnamed mirror contact than to the on-axis vertex. F sits far below its open point on the principal axis. O sits above-left in the outgoing-ray area without a leader. K also lies near the upper contact's row, adding avoidable competing association.

existingMeasuredSupport640.basis: Point screen positions from the exact current spec's 640px frame; label boxes from existing hash-bound preview metadata. These support, but do not replace, the actual visual judgment.

defects.studentImpact: A student cannot safely read which marked point is the curvature center, principal focus, and mirror vertex; the visible P placement suggests the wrong mirror hit. The prose defining O and P does not make detached diagram letters self-identifying.
defects.notClaimed: No assertion is made that the underlying coordinates or paraxial ray counts are wrong. Collision-free text and native PASS are accepted for those limited mechanical checks only.
